# Release Requirements Checklist: Release Publishing

**Purpose**: Validate the quality of the release-publishing requirements —
release mechanics and abort gates, artifact integrity and provenance, and
packaging metadata and documentation — before `/speckit-tasks` turns them into
work.

**Created**: 2026-09-01

**Reviewed**: 2026-09-01

**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the retry path after a failed release attempt specified — the tag already exists at the failed commit, so does retrying require deleting and re-pushing the tag, or moving it? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases "A release fails partway", FR-009]
- [x] CHK002 Are requirements defined for what happens when the already-published check itself cannot complete (network failure, missing token) — does the release fail closed or proceed? [Gap, Spec §FR-025]
- [x] CHK003 Is the required attribution and non-affiliation footer text itself specified or pointed at a definitive source, rather than only asserted to exist? [Gap, Spec §FR-021]
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements stated for what "available as a development tool" means for the type checker — declared as a dependency, invocable, or merely documented? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022]
- [x] CHK005 Does the spec enumerate which project documents repeat the superseded package-index clause, or state how they are found? [Gap, Spec §FR-024]
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for whether the combined checksum file itself carries a provenance record, or is deliberately excluded? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK007 Are the "descriptive fields a released package is expected to have" enumerated exhaustively, or is the list open-ended beyond keywords and classifiers? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK008 Is the disposition of the changelog's own heading line specified — does "the changelog text for that version" include the `## <version>` heading in the release body? [Gap, Spec §FR-002]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK009 Is "clean machine" defined with criteria a reviewer could apply, rather than only contrasted against "a maintainer's working tree"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK010 Is "the full test suite" defined with respect to tests the project normally excludes as long-running? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK011 Is "still marks itself unreleased" defined precisely enough to distinguish a dated heading from an undated one, without assuming a particular date format? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK012 Is "verbatim" scoped unambiguously — does it constrain whitespace, blank-line trimming, and interior markup, or only wording? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK013 Is "a plain checksum a user can verify with no special tooling" quantified, and is "a stock system" defined across the platforms the project supports? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, SC-008]
- [x] CHK014 Does FR-016 say which published artifact the primary installation instruction points at, and whether that instruction pins the released version? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016]
- [x] CHK015 Is FR-018's negation well-formed as a requirement — "No project documentation MUST direct a reader…" reads as a permission rather than a prohibition? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-018]
- [x] CHK016 Is "documented outputs" defined for the drift guard's scope, so a reader can tell which files a stale version fails in? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, FR-013]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK017 Do FR-010 (bump the version when the month has rolled over) and SC-012 (publish `2026.08.1`) still agree, given that the current month is now `2026.09`? [Conflict, Spec §FR-010 vs §SC-012]
- [x] CHK018 Are FR-002's "nothing else may be added" and FR-021's appended footer stated consistently, so the footer is unambiguously an exception rather than a violation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, §FR-021]
- [x] CHK019 Do FR-009's never-reuse rule and the "failed attempt" exception in Edge Cases align on when a version becomes spent — at tag push, or at successful publication? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK020 Is the version's three-spelling model (declared padded, reported unpadded, tagged with `v`) stated consistently across FR-007, FR-012, and the Assumptions? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, §Assumptions "Tag form"]
- [x] CHK021 Do FR-020's type-annotation marker requirement and FR-019's metadata requirement together account for the metadata half of the marker, or is one half unstated? [Consistency, Spec §FR-019, §FR-020]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK022 Can "the release notes body matches the changelog section verbatim" be objectively verified without re-deriving the extraction rule? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK023 Is there a success criterion covering FR-010's month-rollover rule, or does that requirement ship unmeasured? [Coverage, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK024 Is there a success criterion covering FR-021's footer on the published release page, distinct from SC-002's notes-body criterion? [Coverage, Spec §FR-021]
- [x] CHK025 Does a success criterion cover a downloader confirming an artifact's provenance record, as SC-008 does for checksums? [Gap, Spec §SC-008, §FR-006]
- [x] CHK026 Does a success criterion cover FR-019's descriptive metadata and repository links in the built distributions? [Coverage, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK027 Does the contracts' reference to `SC-014` resolve to a criterion that exists in the spec, whose criteria end at SC-013? [Traceability, contracts/package-metadata.md §Guards]
- [x] CHK028 Are the success criteria numbered in a stable order, with SC-013 appearing between SC-009 and SC-010? [Traceability, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [x] CHK029 Is SC-011's "type checker resolves the package's annotations" measurable without mandating a clean type-check run, which FR-022 forbids? [Measurability, Spec §SC-011 vs §FR-022]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK030 Are requirements defined for a changelog section that exists and is dated but whose body is empty? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK031 Are requirements defined for a version heading whose digits are a prefix of another heading's (`2026.08.1` versus `2026.08.10`)? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK032 Are requirements defined for a release published earlier than the newest one — does an older-version hotfix release displace the current release? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK033 Are requirements defined for a tag pushed at a commit on no branch, or at a commit not reachable from the default branch? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK034 Is the ordering of the abort checks specified where two would fail at once, so the reported diagnostic is deterministic? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008, §FR-025]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK035 Is the assumption that the hosting platform's release and attestation features satisfy FR-001 and FR-006 recorded as an assumption rather than as a requirement? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions "Public repository"]
- [x] CHK036 Is the assumption validated that publication is a single indivisible step, which is what makes "nothing is published unless the whole sequence succeeds" hold? [Assumption, Spec §Edge Cases "A release fails partway"]
- [x] CHK037 Is the constitution amendment (FR-023) confirmed as landed, so no requirement here is measured against a superseded clause? [Dependency, Spec §Dependencies]

## Resolutions

Twenty-two items required a change; fifteen were satisfied as written.

### Changed the spec

| Item | Requirement | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CHK001 | Edge Cases | A retry moves the tag onto the corrected commit and pushes it again; an existing tag does not spend a version, only a published release does |
| CHK002 | FR-025 | The already-published check fails closed: an answer it cannot obtain aborts rather than reading as "no release exists" |
| CHK003 | FR-021 | The attribution is the constitution's exact Compatibility-Statement string and the non-affiliation statement one the existing licensing guard recognizes; neither is reworded |
| CHK004 | FR-022 | "Available" is now "declared in the development dependency group", documented with its invoking command, and a clean run is explicitly not a deliverable |
| CHK005 | FR-024 | Scoped to documents describing how the project ships today (README, CONTRIBUTING); `specs/` and `wayfinder/` are historical records, explicitly excluded |
| CHK006 | FR-006 | "Published artifact" means a distribution artifact; the checksum file does not list itself and carries no provenance record |
| CHK008, CHK012, CHK022 | FR-002 | "That changelog text" is the section body, not the heading line; "verbatim" is byte-for-byte with leading and trailing blank lines trimmed and nothing else altered |
| CHK009 | FR-004 | "Clean machine" is provisioned fresh for that run, discarded after, and carries no state from a previous run |
| CHK010 | FR-005 | "Full" excludes nothing; the inner-loop marker and path filters must not be applied |
| CHK011, CHK030 | FR-008 | Blocks unless the heading carries a release date; an undated heading, an unreleased-marked heading, and a dated heading over an empty body each abort |
| CHK015 | FR-018 | Malformed negation fixed to "Project documentation MUST NOT direct a reader…" |
| CHK017 | SC-012 | No longer names `2026.08.1`. The first release carries whatever version is declared when it is tagged, which FR-010 requires to name the current month |
| CHK023 | SC-016 (new) | The contributor documentation's release procedure states the tagging sequence, the dating step, the version-update step, and the month-rollover rule |
| CHK025 | SC-015 (new) | A user verifies a downloaded artifact's provenance record and it names the source commit and the build |
| CHK026, CHK027 | SC-014 (new) | Both formats carry the marker and FR-019's fields and links, established by a packaging guard. This is the criterion `contracts/package-metadata.md` already cited before it existed |
| CHK028 | Success Criteria | SC-013 moved to sit after SC-012; numbering is now monotone |
| CHK029 | SC-011 | Satisfied by the marker being honored, not by zero type-checker errors, which FR-022 forbids requiring |
| CHK031 | Edge Cases | A version heading must never select a longer version whose prefix it is; getting it wrong ships the wrong announcement under a correct version number |

### Changed the design artifacts, to match

- `contracts/release-scripts.md` — preflight gains check 5 (non-empty section
  body); the already-published check becomes check 6 and must distinguish "no
  such release" from "could not ask"; test case 9 added.
- `contracts/release-workflow.md` — step 3 no longer says "the four abort
  conditions".
- `research.md` — R5's check list extended; R18's "exits non-zero → proceed"
  amended, since that reading is exactly what would let a second release be
  published over a first.
- `data-model.md` — Changelog entry validation gains the non-empty-body and
  prefix-collision rules.

### Satisfied as written, no change

- **CHK007** — FR-019 enumerates keywords, classifiers, and the three links.
  `authors` is a plan-level addition that exceeds the requirement rather than
  filling a gap in it.
- **CHK013** — the Assumptions section fixes SHA-256 as "the algorithm whose
  verification utility ships on every supported platform", and research R7
  gives the command per platform.
- **CHK014** — FR-012's "the normalized unpadded form where the artifact
  filename appears" already establishes that the command names a specific
  pinned artifact file. Which of the two formats it names is an implementation
  choice, correctly left below spec altitude.
- **CHK016** — the guard's scope is the existing guard's glob, and the
  Assumptions section says so, deliberately without fixing a file count.
- **CHK018** — FR-002 already names the footer as the one thing appended, so
  it reads as the stated exception rather than a contradiction.
- **CHK019** — FR-009 puts the transition at publication and states the
  failed-attempt exception in the same breath.
- **CHK020** — FR-007, FR-012, the Assumptions, and the "declared and reported
  strings differ in form" edge case agree on all three spellings.
- **CHK021** — FR-020's "advertise that it ships type annotations" covers both
  halves; the marker file is the mechanism, not the whole requirement.
- **CHK032** — the never-reuse rule plus monotone CalVer increments make an
  older-version release a case the project does not support.
  `contracts/release-workflow.md` records the matching decision to pass no
  `--latest` flag either way.
- **CHK033** — the tagged commit is the authority by construction (FR-004,
  FR-007). Branch reachability is deliberately not a gate: the tag is the
  deliberate act, and the full suite runs at that commit regardless.
- **CHK034** — research R5 fixes the check order and gives the reason. A
  design-artifact answer is the right altitude for it.
- **CHK035** — the Assumptions section records the hosting platform as an
  assumption, with its release feature and its attestation feature named
  separately.
- **CHK036** — held structurally, not by assumption: publication is one
  `gh release create` call and it is the last step
  (`contracts/release-workflow.md`).
- **CHK037** — constitution 2026.08.2, amended 2026-08-31. The Development
  Workflow section now defines a release as a tagged bundle on the public
  source repository and carries the never-reuse rule.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- **Operational consequence of CHK017**: the requirements are now consistent,
  but the project still declares `2026.08.1` with a `## 2026.08.1
  (unreleased)` changelog heading, and the month has rolled over. FR-010 makes
  bumping to a version naming the current month a step the maintainer takes
  before tagging, not something this feature's implementation does. Whoever
  cuts the first release does it then, taking the changelog heading and every
  documented occurrence with it.
